subject: mathematics
question_text: Find the domain and the range of the real valued function f(x) = log|4 − x²|.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.13, chapter 2 FUNCTIONS, Very Short Answer question 20(i). Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The question asks for two things, so the 1+1 shape gives one mark to the domain and one to the range, and the range mark is for the values of |4 − x²| being found, not for the word R on its own. Paper position: Maths-1A Section A runs Q1–Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find both the domain and the range here — what the log needs, and how you get at the range.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find the domain
steps.margin_note: First mark is R − {−2, 2}. Both points must go, and the reason must be that the input of a log has to be positive.
steps.memory_tip: With a modulus inside a log, the modulus fixes the sign, so only the zeros are removed. Solve 4 − x² = 0.
lines: log t is real only when t > 0.

recall.must_convey: That the log needs a positive input, so |4 − x²| > 0, which removes only x = 2 and x = −2.
accept: log needs a positive input so the modulus must not be zero
four minus x squared must not be zero so x is not plus or minus two
the modulus is never negative so only the zeros are removed
log lo positive value undali kabatti x plus or minus two kaakudadu
the domain is all real numbers except two and minus two
reject: solve four minus x squared greater than zero

steps.why: A logarithm is real only for a positive input. The modulus already makes 4 − x² positive whenever it is not zero, so the inequality |4 − x²| > 0 removes nothing except the two roots of 4 − x² = 0. Solving 4 − x² > 0 instead would wrongly throw away everything outside (−2, 2).
common_mistakes: Solving 4 − x² > 0 and giving (−2, 2); the modulus has already fixed the sign.
Removing only x = 2 and forgetting x = −2.
Writing the domain as R, as if a log accepted 0.

steps.label: Find the range
steps.margin_note: Second mark is the range R, with the values of |4 − x²| shown first. A bare 'Range = R' with no working is where this mark is lost.
steps.memory_tip: Find the values the inside takes, then read the log of them. The inside covers (0, ∞), so the log covers R.
lines: Put t = |4 − x²|, so f(x) = log t.
So t takes every positive value.
As t runs over (0, ∞), log t runs over R.

recall.must_convey: That |4 − x²| takes every positive value on the domain, so log of it takes every real value, giving range R.
accept: the modulus takes every positive value so the log takes every real value
inside two the value is up to four and outside two it grows without limit
t covers zero to infinity so log t covers all real numbers
lopala value covers all positive numbers kabatti range R
the range is all of R
reject: the range is zero to infinity

steps.why: The range needs its own work; it does not follow from the domain. Inside the domain |4 − x²| gets as close to 0 as we like near x = ±2, equals 4 at x = 0, and grows without limit as |x| grows, so it reaches every positive number. The logarithm of every positive number covers all of R, so the range is R.
common_mistakes: Giving the range as (0, ∞), which is the range of |4 − x²|, not of its logarithm.
Writing 'Range = R' with no working; the values of the inside have to be found first.
Stopping at t ∈ (0, 4] and missing the values from |x| > 2.
